newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian states maintain credit quality - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Australian states maintain credit quality - S&P.

text.p: The debt burdens of Australian states should decline further in fiscal 1997 to June 30, auguring well for their ratings in the medium term, ratings agency Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday.

"The Australian states consolidated their rating positions in fiscal 1996 with very strong financial performances and continue to demonstrate sound financial fundamentals into fiscal 1997," S&P said in its monthly CreditFocus publication.

The agency noted that since June last year the local currency ratings of the Australian Capital Territory, Queensland and New South Wales had been affirmed while Victoria's rating was upgraded to AA-plus from AA.
The ratings for South Australia and Western Australia are still under review and the Northern Territory is not rated.

"Sound ongoing finances, declining debt, assisted by privatisations, and the persistance of the differences among the states of some of the non-financial rating factors, are the main features emerging from the reviews of the states over the past 12 months," S&P said.
The ongoing financial position of the public sector as a whole in each state was sound, it said.
S&P said the Australian Capital Territory was the only jurisdiction with an underlying deficit in fiscal 1996. All other states either recorded a balance or surplus for the year.
